body:
## Problem

With `'wrap'`, a line whose cells are hidden by conceal still wraps at its pre-conceal columns (the historical "boguscols" padding): the display hides the concealed cells, but the line keeps its original screen height, and the cursor, `screenpos()`, `wincol()`, mouse, and `gj`/`gk` all use pre-conceal columns.

This is the decade-old #14409 (inherited from vim/vim#260). Only the `virt_lines` part of #18282 shipped in 0.13; the conceal-reflow part did not.

## Solution

Make `'wrap'` conceal-aware end-to-end: a line with hidden cells reflows to its displayed width, and every geometry consumer follows the reflowed layout.

- `plines`: split screen-layout width from virtual width (via a shared `ConcealWalk` helper); reflow persistent extmark conceal.
- `screenpos()`, mouse click position/`getmousepos()`, `curs_columns()`/`winline()`/`wincol()`, and `gj`/`gk`/`g0`/`g^`/`gm`/`g$` follow the reflowed screen column.
- New `_on_conceal` decoration-provider callback: tree-sitter `@conceal` materialises into the marktree, so it reflows too.
- Force a full redraw when a concealed cursor line changes height, avoiding a TUI stale-cell scroll artifact (mirrors the existing `conceal_lines` guard).

Virtual columns stay conceal-neutral (`virtcol()`, `w_curswant` for `j`/`k`, `|`, Visual, the `getvcol` API); only screen-position consumers change.

Scope: covers conceal from extmarks and `treesitter-highlight-conceal`. `matchadd()`-style ephemeral conceal does **not** reflow, and legacy regex `:syntax` conceal (e.g., for TeX) is unchanged.

Ref #14409
Recreated from (now closed) PR #40881
Design references: #10442 #18282, vim/vim#260 vim/vim#9443 vim/vim#10442 vim/vim#20472

## Notes

- Unrelated bug found while testing this (`TSHighlighter.new()` leaking callbacks when `start()` is called twice on an active buffer): fixed separately in #41090.
- Tests in `conceal_wrap_spec.lua` hold what doesn't map to an existing file: core reflow mechanics, motions combined with conceal, tree-sitter materialization, undo/redo, multi-window.

This may be personal preference, but I prefer writing emojis in code with `\u{XXXX}` notation instead of literally in-lining the emoji in the test. Doesn't really matter tho.

> EDIT: realized this is actually useful in this scenario

--     were visible, so it takes 2 screen rows: row 1 ends mid-blank and
--     " World!" gets pushed down alone onto row 2, even though almost
--     nothing is actually drawn there.
--   - this branch (AFTER): the line reflows to what's actually DISPLAYED.
--     "Hello, … World!" is only ~16 cells wide, so it fits entirely on ONE
--     row -- no wasted second row.
--

--   - Put the cursor on row 1 col 1, then press `gj` -- BEFORE it jumps to
--     the (mostly blank) second screen row; AFTER there's nothing to jump
--     to, since the line no longer wraps.
--   - `:echo screenpos(win_getid(), 1, 60)` -- the reported screen row for
--     column 60 ("World!") differs between the two.
--   - `:vertical resize 25` / `:vertical resize 60` -- reflow updates live.

vim.cmd('silent! only')
vim.o.conceallevel = 2
vim.o.concealcursor = 'nvic'

It looks like `screenpos()` misreports the screen row for a buffer position immediately following inline virtual text that spans a wrap boundary. I don't want to file a bug report yet until I can get confirmation.

Root cause: in `charsize_regular()` (plines.c), a virtual text mark's width gets bundled into the same character's `CharSize.width` at its anchor column -- so `getvcol()` (which sums widths while walking toward a target column) excludes that virtual text's width until after the anchor character is fully processed, even though the virtual text visually renders before it.

# Bug: stale/incorrect glyph on a line with combining characters after the cursor leaves it, in a real terminal, with 'concealcursor' revealing/concealing that line

## Summary

When 'concealcursor' causes a line to reveal while the cursor is on it and re-conceal
when the cursor leaves (the normal, long-standing 'concealcursor' behavior -- this does
NOT require any specific conceal content on the line itself), a real terminal can end up
showing a corrupted character on that line immediately after the cursor moves off it. The
line's actual buffer text is unchanged; this is a pure rendering bug. It does not reproduce
via Nvim's own `--embed`/`ext_linegrid` clients (e.g. GUIs, or the test suite's Screen
harness) -- only through the built-in TUI writing to a real terminal -- which means the
bug is in the TUI's incremental terminal-output/redraw path (`src/nvim/tui/tui.c`), not in
Nvim's internal grid computation.

## Environment

- Reproduced on Nvim commit `9180c6e093` (early July 2026 master), Windows 11, Windows
  Terminal / ConPTY. Not yet tested on Linux/macOS terminals, but the bug is in
  terminal-output code, not OS-specific drawing, so it likely reproduces there too.
- `conceallevel=3`, `concealcursor=` (empty -- cursor line is always revealed, in every
  mode), `wrap` on, in a narrow window (25 columns).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Save a file containing (at minimum) these two lines somewhere with other concealable
   markdown content in the buffer (see note below on why other content is needed):
   ```
   - Precomposed: café, naïve, Ångström
   - Decomposed: café, naïve, Ångström
   ```
   (The "Decomposed" line's `naïve` should be typed with the `i` and combining
   diaeresis U+0308 as separate code points, rather than precomposed `ï` U+00EF -- both
   display identically and take the same number of screen cells.)
2. Open the file in a real terminal (not a GUI/embedded client):
   `nvim --clean -c "set conceallevel=3 concealcursor= wrap" file.md`, in a window ~25
   columns wide.
3. Enable markdown tree-sitter highlighting if not automatic
   (`:lua vim.treesitter.start()`), so `b_marktree->n_keys > 0` (conceal exists
   *somewhere* in the buffer -- required for the "Decomposed" line, which has no conceal
   of its own, to go through the same code path as concealed lines).
4. Move the cursor with `j`/`k` so it lands exactly on the "Decomposed" line, then move
   off it (either direction, e.g. one more `j`).

## Expected behavior

The "Decomposed" line's text is rendered identically before, during, and after the
cursor visits it (nothing on that line is actually concealed, so 'concealcursor'
shouldn't change its rendered content at all).

## Actual behavior

The instant the cursor moves off that line, one character silently changes on the real
terminal: `naïve` renders as `naï,e` (the `v` is replaced by `,`). Moving the cursor back
onto the line re-renders it correctly; moving off again reproduces the corruption. This
is 100% deterministic in our testing.

Confirmed the buffer's actual text never changes (checked via
`nvim_buf_get_lines()` before/after) -- this is purely a stale/incorrect terminal cell,
not a text-editing bug.

## Why this points at tui.c specifically

The identical repro run through Nvim's own `--embed` UI protocol (i.e., applying the
exact same `grid_line`/`grid_scroll` events Nvim emits, via the functional test suite's
plain `Screen` harness, which is a reference re-implementation of the grid, not a real
terminal) never shows the corruption -- confirming Nvim's internal state and the events
it emits are correct. The corruption only appears when those same events are converted
into real terminal escape sequences and interpreted by an actual terminal, i.e. in the
TUI client's own output-diffing logic in `src/nvim/tui/tui.c` (`print_cell_at_pos`,
`UGRID_FOREACH_CELL`, and the cursor-position/skip-cell bookkeeping around them),
likely a column/cell-count bug specific to a row containing a zero-width combining
character when only part of that row is being incrementally rewritten (as opposed to a
fresh full-line paint).

## Suggested next steps for whoever picks this up

- Try to reproduce with plain ASCII (no combining characters) at the same
  cursor-line-reveal-toggle boundary, to determine whether combining characters are
  actually required to trigger it, or just happen to make the corruption visually obvious.
- Instrument/log the exact bytes tui.c writes to the pty for the affected row across the
  "cursor enters" -> "cursor leaves" transition, to catch the incorrect column skip/write
  directly.

**EDIT: This analysis is exploring no wrap and no conceal settings to determine if any hot path or normal path code paths are affected by this PR.**

**TLDR; conceallevel=0 and nowrap is essentially identical performance. conceallevel>0 + wrap has some performance cost which is expected and I elaborated on in an earlier comment.**

I reviewed the gating logic at every hot-path call site added as part of this work (`plines.c`, `drawline.c`, `move.c`, `normal.c`, `mouse.c`, `decoration.c`, and `highlighter.lua`).

`conceallevel=0` + `nowrap`: effectively identical performance. Every conceal-aware code path is gated behind a cheap `w_p_cole > 0` (or equivalent) check that short-circuits immediately:

* `init_charsize_arg()`'s `maybe_conceal` starts with `wp->w_p_cole > 0 &&` -- false in one comparison, so it never touches the marktree/provider checks.
* `linesize_fast()' / `charsize_fast()` (the common-case width functions) are 100% untouched -- unchanged from before this feature.
* `drawline.c`'s reflow logic lives inside the pre-existing `else if (wp->w_p_cole > 0 && is_concealing)` branch -- never entered.
* `decor_conceal_materialise()` returns after 2 comparisons (`w_p_cole < 1`) before even checking for providers.
* gj/gk, g0/g^/gm/g$ (`normal.c`) compute `use_scol = w_p_cole > 0 && ...` and ternary-select the old cheap function when false.
* Two spots (`screenpos()`'s `conceal_off_before()`, mouse's `scol_to_col()`) call the new functions unconditionally rather than gating at the call site, but those functions self-degrade internally via the same cheap check, and neither is a per-keystroke hot loop (one-off API call / one call per click).

`conceallevel>0` + `wrap`: performance overhead likely but not "noticeable" interactively. Per redrawn/measured line you now pay: one decoration-provider-list scan (`decor_conceal_materialise`, typically 0–3 providers), and a per-character marktree hidden-width lookup (`linesize_conceal_hidden`) during the same O(line length) walk that already existed — no new algorithmic complexity, just extra constant work per character. If tree-sitter `@conceal` is involved, materializing also invokes a Lua callback and a `tree:parse(true)` per row (cached, so cheap on repeat). This scales with concealed+wrapped line length/count, so it could add up on pathological cases (huge single lines, thousands of concealed lines scrolled rapidly), but it's linear, not quadratic.
